title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini in two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired Δ = 0.015; preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.035]. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes referencing archived artifact checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and to assist NetOps automation. Operational safety and correctness require more than syntactic plausibility: preservation of invariants, bounded blast radius, and auditable decision trails. A common architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes configuration(s), a deterministic verifier checks policy and functional invariants, and an automated repair routine attempts correction. While prior work shows feasibility for LLM‑based configuration generation, quantitative evidence for operational benefit from verifier insertion under preregistered confirmatory designs with full provenance is limited.

Research question and contributions. We ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded multi‑vendor synthetic benchmark? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) comparing baseline (LLM‑alone) to guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair); (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle with per‑episode verifier traces and provider call artifacts (canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); (3) preregistered confirmatory inference (exact McNemar and bootstrap percentile CIs) and deterministic reproduction recipes (script paths and invocations); (4) artifact‑grounded failure analysis explaining why the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy threshold was not met and operational recommendations.
sections.related_work: Tool‑assisted correction and verifier literature. Tool‑augmented critique (e.g., CRITIC) and verifier‑based repair motivate closed‑loop pipelines where deterministic checks serve as corrective oracles. Formal and ensemble verification work (e.g., SymNet, model‑checking approaches) illustrates rigorous reachability and policy validation for network invariants. Recent applied NetOps studies (PreConfig, intent engines, intent translation) demonstrate LLM feasibility but highlight correctness and safety gaps that motivate verifier insertion. Survey and benchmark work on LLMs for NetOps documents desiderata—auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets—and reports ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is high. Our study differs by preregistering a single primary estimand and analysis plan, executing a paired within‑task design with full archived provenance, and providing deterministic reproduction recipes tied to artifact checksums.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified the primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed from the deterministic validator correctness indicator. H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling, the exact primary test (exact McNemar two‑sided) and the CI method (bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The preregistration and execution manifest are archived.

Synthetic benchmark and task generation. We used a deterministic Cornetto‑like multi‑vendor task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). The confirmatory sample (200 paired tasks) was stratified across topology scales (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were deterministically excluded prior to confirmatory sampling. Each task includes initial_state, expected_final_state, allowed_touched_fields, required_sequence, and difficulty metadata; these are the ground truth for functional checks and are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865).

Execution semantics and guarding. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Each pair used a single shared initial candidate generation (shared_initial) as prespecified: the same initial LLM candidate was scored under both conditions to isolate verifier/repair effects. In the guarded condition the pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if violations were reported the pipeline issued at most one automated repair invocation (preregistered maximum repair calls = 1). The verifier emits structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) including parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and difficulty pattern; these traces are archived and drive correctness scoring (deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scorer rules archived with responses).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete_pairs included in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12. Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3). Canonical per‑episode archive: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete pairs n = 188). The preregistered paired contingency (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) is: n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded only), n_01 = 0 (baseline only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate success rates: baseline = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded = 188/188 = 1.0; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Paired bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729; preregistered) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records seed and resamples; SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc).

Sensitivity analysis — preregistered bootstrap (both‑missing→failures). Treating the 12 both‑missing pairs as failures yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; paired Δ = 0.015. We computed the preregistered bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) deterministically from the archived per‑pair outcomes and obtained [0.0, 0.035]. Reproducible invocation (artifact‑bundled scripts): 1) extract per‑pair NDJSON:
  python3 execution/tools/extract_pairs.py --input execution/raw_results.jsonl --output analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson
  (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7)
 2) run bootstrap:
  python3 execution/tools/bootstrap_delta.py --input analysis/pairs_slice.ndjson --seed 1729 --resamples 10000 --missing-as-failure --output analysis/bootstrap_result.json
  The above two‑line recipe reproduces the preregistered sensitivity CI bit‑for‑bit from the archived raw_results.jsonl; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records parameters and seed (SHA‑256 above).

Repair invocation provenance. Repair invocations were rare (stage_counts.repair = 3) and correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). All repair invocation metadata (episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, final score) are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl. Deterministic extraction command (artifact‑bundled jq available in the bundle):
  jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path, repair_provider_trace_sha256, score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json
Run the above to produce analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json (lossless slice) that enumerates the three repair calls and the provider_call filenames (relative to execution/provider_calls/) along with their SHA‑256 checksums. The provider_call files referenced by repair_provider_trace_path live under execution/provider_calls/ in the artifact bundle and can be cross‑checked by SHA‑256. We intentionally do not duplicate those filenames here to avoid transcription errors; execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) is the canonical source and the jq extraction yields a bit‑for‑bit verifiable slice.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and drivers. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. This effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and not statistically significant at α = 0.05. Two artifact‑grounded operational drivers explain the result: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and sampled tasks often produced LLM proposals that already matched golden configurations or passed validation, so repair was rarely invoked (repair invocations = 3).

Failure‑mode diagnostics. The three repair cases that drove n_10 were inspected via their verifier traces archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl; each shows a small sequence correction (missing ordering or a transient shutdown/restore step) that the automated repair inserted. The verifier traces include difficulty summaries (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern) explaining why a single automated repair sufficed in these episodes. Where repairs were not invoked the shared initial candidate already satisfied full_intent_constraint_validation: validator traces show violation_count = 0 and valid = true.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial generation isolates verifier/repair effects but creates dependence accounted for by paired tests. Construct validity: the success metric is the deterministic validator output and depends on verifier coverage; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded deterministically (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 listed above). External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and single verifier limit generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) reduce power to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp threshold.

Operational implications and recommendations. (1) Use verifier insertion primarily for auditability and to generate deterministic traces when baseline model correctness is already high. (2) To demonstrate measurable operational gains, increase task difficulty or expand verifier coverage so repairs are invoked more frequently. (3) Increase permitted repair iterations beyond one for complex dependency patterns and archive iterative traces to study repair convergence and blast‑radius dynamics. (4) Evaluate across multiple LLMs and verifier implementations to establish generality.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Repairs were infrequent (3 invocations) and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes so others can reproduce the preregistered sensitivity CI and enumerate repair invocations from the canonical archives.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.
